ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The bonds do not match the angles.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three carbon atoms labeled C, which are connected by C-C bonds to form a triangular ring; each carbon atom is also connected to two H atoms. The question stem states that this triangle is an equilateral triangle. Reasoning: Each interior angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, so the C-C-C bond angle in the ring is forced to be close to 60°. But the usually more stable tetrahedral bond angle of a saturated carbon atom is about 109.5°. Therefore, the ring structure compresses the carbon-carbon bonds into positions that do not conform to the normal bonding angle of carbon atoms, producing angle strain, so cyclopropane is relatively unstable.
